# MPkWh.com

> MPkWh.com ranks the most efficient electric cars available in the US by miles per kWh (Mi/kWh) — the EV equivalent of MPG. Data is sourced from official EPA fuel economy ratings and updated weekly every Monday.

## What is Mi/kWh?

Miles per kilowatt-hour (Mi/kWh) measures how far an electric vehicle travels on one unit of electricity. A higher number means greater efficiency: lower energy consumption, lower running costs, and longer range from the same battery. It is the direct EV equivalent of miles per gallon (MPG) for combustion vehicles. Mi/kWh is derived from the EPA's MPGe rating divided by 33.7 (the kWh-energy equivalent of one gallon of gasoline).

## Notes

- Efficiency figures reflect the most efficient trim and configuration available for each model year.
- Not all 2026 models have received EPA ratings yet. The table is updated every Monday as new ratings are published.
- Cost-per-100-miles uses the latest US average residential electricity rate published monthly by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA). As of June 2026: $0.1805/kWh (March 2026 figure, published May 2026).
- Data source: US EPA fueleconomy.gov
